Conclusions (II) : Some phones are vaults.

(II) Some phones are vaults - Doesn't follow** **(Their is no direct relation between phones and vaults may be it is possible but not definite. Hence, it is false)

**Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.**

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 3."**

If ‘A’ stands for ‘÷’, ‘B’ stands for ‘×’, ‘C’ stands for ‘+’ and ‘D’ stands for ‘−’, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

1 D 40 A 7 B 7 C 46 = ?
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7751840ca1840d12cadc428f84d30e2cdcd5e7f82d52a57de21f2404c58eed88.png] 

**According to the given information:**

 
 

 **Letter**
 A
 B
 C
 D
 
 

 **Sign**
 ÷
 ×
 +
 −
 
 

 

**Given Expression:** 1 D 40 A 7 B 7 C 46 = ?

Replacing the letters with signs and using the BODMAS rule:

**= 1 − 40 ÷ 7 × 7 + 46**

= 1 − 40 + 46

 

**= **1 + 46 − 40

= 47 − 40

= 7

Hence, the correct answer is "**option 1"**

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.
(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
(53, 47, 35)
(117, 111, 99)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic: Second Number = First Number − 6; Third Number = Second Number − 12**

For the first set **(53, 47, 35)**

⇒ 53 − 6 = 47

⇒ 47 − 12 = 35.

For the second set **(117, 111, 99)**

⇒ 117 − 6 = 111

⇒ 111 − 12 = 99.

Applying the same logic to the set in **Option 3**

**(212, 206, 194)**

⇒ 212 − 6 = 206

⇒ 206 − 12 = 194.

Hence, the correct answer is **'Option 3'**.

questions.question:
Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7751840ca1840d12cadc428f84d30e2cdcd5e7f82d52a57de21f2404c58eed88.png] 

The logic followed here is to interchange the given numbers and verify the equation using the **BODMAS** rule.

**Given equation:** (21 × 2) ÷ 3 + 15 × 5 − 19 × 4 + 36 + 7 × 6 = 57

**For Option (1): Interchanging 4 and 5**

After interchanging numbers **4** and **5**, the equation becomes:

(21 × 2) ÷ 3 + 15 × **4** − 19 × **5** + 36 + 7 × 6 = 57

__
 
• LHS = (42) ÷ 3 __+ 15 × 4 − 19 × 5 + 36 + 7 × 6 
 
• LHS = 14 + __15 × 4 __− __19 × 5__ + 36 + 42
 
• LHS = 14 + 60 + 36 + 42 − 95
 
• LHS = 74 + 36 + 42 − 95 
 
• LHS = −21 __+ 36 + 42__
 
• LHS = __15 + 42__
 
• LHS = 57

Comparing LHS with Right Hand Side (RHS):

 
• **57 = 57**
 
• **LHS = RHS**

 

Hence, the correct answer is "**option 1"**

questions.question: Raman ranked 25th from the top and 67th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in his class?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

 
• Rank of **Raman** from the **top** = 25th
 
• Rank of **Raman** from the **bottom** = 67th

**Total number of students** = (Rank from the Top + Rank from the Bottom) − 1

= (25 + 67) − 1

= 92 − 1

= 91

There are **91** students in the class.

Hence, the correct answer is **'Option 2'**.
